blocks.text: The integrated terminal is a central component of your development workflow in Cursor. Since Cursor is a fork of Visual Studio Code, it shares the same foundational architecture and keybindings. This familiarity makes switching to Cursor straightforward for developers who already use VS Code.
Using keyboard shortcuts to open terminal in Cursor on Mac

Keyboard shortcuts are the fastest way to manage your interface. For the terminal, the shortcut is Control + `. Note that this uses the Control key, not the Command key. This is a common point of confusion for Mac users who are used to Command-based shortcuts.
Navigating menus to launch the terminal

If you prefer using the mouse or are working in a situation where keyboard shortcuts are inconvenient, the menu bar is always available. Simply click View in the top menu bar, then select Terminal from the dropdown list.

Sometimes the terminal may not appear or may remain blank. This is often due to shell configuration or environment path issues. Start by restarting the Cursor application completely. If that does not work, check your terminal profile settings.

items: Ensure your shell (zsh or bash) is correctly installed and accessible.
Check that your PATH variable is properly set in your shell configuration file.
Verify that Cursor has the necessary permissions to access your project folder.
Try switching your default terminal profile in the Cursor settings menu.

blocks.text: Why Cursor terminal behaves like VS Code

Cursor maintains compatibility with the VS Code ecosystem. This includes support for the same terminal profiles and extensions. You can run any command in the Cursor terminal that you would run in your standard Mac Terminal app or the VS Code terminal.

The Cursor desktop application provides a full, local terminal experience. In contrast, web-based or mobile versions of similar tools often rely on cloud orchestration. These environments may not provide the same level of access to your local file system or shell environment as the desktop app.

faq.question: Why does the terminal shortcut use Control instead of Command?
faq.answer: Cursor inherits the default keybindings from VS Code, which uses the Control key for the terminal toggle to avoid conflicts with common Mac system shortcuts.

faq.question: Can I change the terminal shortcut in Cursor?
faq.answer: Yes, you can customize keyboard shortcuts by opening the Command Palette with Cmd + Shift + P, typing Keyboard Shortcuts, and searching for the Toggle Terminal command.

faq.question: What should I do if my terminal is blank?
faq.answer: First, verify that your default shell is set correctly in settings. If the issue persists, ensure your shell configuration files like .zshrc or .bash_profile are free of syntax errors that might prevent the terminal from initializing.

steps.name: Use the Keyboard Shortcut
steps.text: Press the Control key and the backtick key (`) at the same time to toggle the terminal panel.

steps.name: Use the Menu Bar
steps.text: Click on View in the top menu bar, then select Terminal from the list.

steps.name: Use the Command Palette
steps.text: Open the Command Palette, type Toggle Terminal, and press Return.

troubleshooting.fix: Restart Cursor and check your terminal profile settings.

troubleshooting.problem: Terminal is blank or shows error
troubleshooting.fix: Verify your shell path and check for errors in your shell configuration file.
